title: Home First Finance Company India Ltd - 543259 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Home First Q2 FY27 AUM rose 27% YoY to Rs 18,010 crore and PAT grew 29.1% YoY to Rs 170 crore, with Stage 3 down to 1.7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth: disbursements of Rs 1,705 crore (+32.2% YoY, +4.7% QoQ) and AUM up 6.3% QoQ. PAT of Rs 170 crore rose 6.5% QoQ, with ROE up 40 bps to 14.9% and cost-to-income down to 30.8% from 32.7%. Gross Stage 3 improved 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and credit cost was 40 bps. Management reiterated a 5.0-5.2% spread commitment, a 25% AUM growth target for FY27 (Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027), and exit ROE targets of 15% (FY27) and 16% (FY28). Co-lending disbursements collapsed to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 46 crore in Q1, which management attributed to RBI guideline implementation delays.

financial_highlights.change: Stage 3 +10 bps QoQ; DPD flat QoQ

Net worth / book value per share

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh grew strongly YoY in H1; UP, Rajasthan, NCR and Karnataka recorded strong YoY growth. Tamil Nadu returned to growth with +12% in Q2 after being marginally down in H1.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Individual housing loans are 84% of the portfolio. LAP is kept within a 20% non-housing guardrail and is running at a slower pace; management sees about 5% headroom worth 6-7 bps of spread.

segments.name: Customer segments by property type
segments.commentary: Apartments including developer-led row houses are about 30% of AUM, self-construction about 30%, plots 1-2%, and repair and renovation about 1%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of about 25% for FY27, implying Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027; management flagged a possible 1-2% upside from tailwinds.
Exit ROE target of 15% for FY27 and 16% for FY28 (March 2028); management said current momentum could exceed these.
Spread maintained at 5.0-5.2% on a fully floating book; PLR to be raised only when borrowing cost moves by about 10-15 bps.
Opex-to-assets to fall 10 bps YoY, with FY27 target of about 2.6%.
Gross NPA target around 1.7% and credit cost around 40 bps.
Insurance distribution fee draft circular estimated at about 35 bps ROA hit; about 10 bps may be conceded back, leaving 20-25 bps to offset via LAP mix, assignment income and pricing or fee changes.
Co-lending transactions expected to pick up in Q3 FY27.
Branch additions of 10-15 in the next two quarters, taking the run-rate to 20-25 per year.
capex_capacity: Network at 181 branches and 379 touch points after adding 6 branches in Q2; about 10 branches added in FY27 so far, with 10-15 more planned over the next two quarters.
Annual branch addition run-rate of 20-25; 1-2 underperforming branches are closed each year as business as usual, including recent closures in Rajasthan.

Technology: four in-house AI tools live (Cue, ClariFi, BankLens, DocIQ); over the next 18 months plans to move to a single shared data and decision platform and extend AI into sourcing, collections and servicing.
UP growth push planned for next year, with team strengthening on track.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is good across the board; rejection rates are steady and no change in leads-to-disbursement conversion.
Average new origination ticket size is about Rs 15-16 lakh; top-up is 2-3% of disbursements.
Balance transfer outflows reduced to about 4.5% from 5-6%; management guides a 4-6% range.
Origination yield ex co-lending stable at 13%; management says yield compression in the Rs 25 lakh+ segment is insignificant.
Portfolio yield fell about 10 bps QoQ to 13%, attributed to passing lower rates to new customers earlier.
Southern markets are slower because of self-construction-led demand, which takes several quarters to convert into disbursements.
Around 30% of borrowings are linked to external benchmarks; a 25 bps repo hike translates to about 10 bps in borrowing cost over time.
Hedging cost on ECB via cross-currency swaps is about 3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to drought-declared districts in MP and Gujarat, and impact on disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gujarat and MP asset quality has been consistent and better than national numbers; customers are mainly in manufacturing and services, so drought impact is not seen as significant. Individual credit calls will be taken if agriculture dependence is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will spreads improve with rising rates given history of 5.5% spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 5.0-5.2% spread; 5.5%+ was only a short post-COVID phase when borrowing costs fell sharply and was not considered sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for PLR hike and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLR hike yet since borrowing costs have not moved; will reprice once borrowing cost transmits, following RBI draft guidelines. Management expects about 20 bps of cost transmission from a 50 bps cumulative repo move over 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of insurance distribution fee draft circular?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated ROA impact of about 35 bps; about 10 bps may be conceded back by insurers, leaving 20-25 bps to recover via more LAP, more assignments, and pricing or fee changes.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending volumes fell sharply in Q2; what is happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay due to implementing new RBI guidelines with partners; management expects a visible uptick in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost decline QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campus hiring is concentrated in Q1 and Q4, so Q2 and Q3 have fewer joiners; management reiterated 2.6% opex-to-assets for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CEO succession position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no such conversation; the CEO's term runs to July 2028 and he is available for reappointment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tamil Nadu and other southern markets lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Southern markets are largely self-construction driven with slower staged disbursements; leadership gaps in Tamil Nadu have been filled and growth is expected to reverse over the next two quarters.

risks_watch: Rising rate cycle: management said a 10-15 bps borrowing cost move is needed before PLR changes, so margin pressure may persist in the interim.
Insurance distribution fee draft circular: 20-25 bps of ROA to recover through levers that are not yet executed.
Co-lending recovery in Q3 is dependent on RBI guideline implementation with partners.
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh/Telangana growth remains sub-teens or single digit, and management expects a reversal only over the next two quarters.
Stage 3 provision coverage ECL-only at 23.6%, with ECL assumptions now recalibrated quarterly and a slight uptick noted in the quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and demand, with a clear Q3 uptick narrative. More guarded on rates and insurance-fee impact, where management is open about needing levers and a repricing trigger.

We don't see as such any risk in the numbers that we are talking about.

There is no such conversation going on anywhere.

adds.what: Branch network additions: 10-15 more branches over the next two quarters (network at 181 branches after 6 added in Q2; about 10 added in FY27 so far)

growth.why: Management reiterated a ~25% AUM growth target for FY27 (Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027, possible 1-2% upside), backed by Q2 disbursements up 32.2% YoY and 10-15 branch additions over the next two quarters, but no order-book or detailed capacity numbers beyond branches, and co-lending disbursements collapsed to Rs 1.8 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread held at 5.0-5.2% with NIM 6.0% and cost of borrowing ~7.8% vs incremental 7.5%; management says 5.5%+ is not sustainable and PLR only moves once borrowing cost rises 10-15 bps, while ~30% of borrowings are benchmark-linked (25 bps repo hike = ~10 bps cost), and insurance fee change could cost ~35 bps ROA with only 10 bps conceded back.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network at 181 branches after 6 added in Q2, with 10-15 more branches planned over the next two quarters and a 20-25 per year run-rate; branch additions are firmly under way.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets ~25% AUM growth for FY27 (Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027, possible 1-2% upside) after Q2 disbursements rose 32.2% YoY to Rs 1,705 crore, though co-lending disbursements fell to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 46 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a possible 1-2% AUM upside and said current momentum could exceed the 15% FY27 and 16% FY28 exit ROE targets, but these are conditional on tailwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Insurance distribution fee draft circular could cut ROA by ~35 bps with only 20-25 bps recoverable through levers not yet executed, and co-lending recovery in Q3 depends on partners implementing RBI guidelines.

rows.label: Insurance distribution fee draft circular
rows.why: Estimated ~35 bps ROA hit, with ~10 bps expected to be conceded back, leaving 20-25 bps to offset via LAP mix, assignments, and pricing or fee changes that are not yet executed.

rows.label: Co-lending pickup in Q3 FY27
rows.why: Co-lending disbursements fell to Rs 1.8 crore in Q2 from Rs 46 crore in Q1 on RBI guideline delays; management expects a visible uptick in Q3, but the book is only Rs 593 crore (3.3% of AUM).

rows.label: Tamil Nadu and southern growth reversal
rows.why: Tamil Nadu grew 12% in Q2 after lagging in H1 and leadership gaps are filled, but Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and Tamil Nadu remain sub-teens or single digit and self-construction disbursements take several quarters to convert.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM growth, asset quality (Stage 3 down to 1.7%) and demand, while guarded on rate-cycle margin pass-through and the insurance distribution fee impact; analysts pressed on spreads, PLR repricing, and co-lending and southern-market slowdowns.
